statement: A 16-cell reservoir service runs on reservoir:1337 (a copy of the binary ships in /work/reservoir/). Pour allocates a cell with one of seven fixed byte sizes (40, 152, 984, 1000, 1032, 1048, 1560) and no other size is accepted; drain frees a cell but the service never forgets its pointer; poke copies attacker-supplied bytes (1 to 512 of them) to any cell plus an arbitrary offset 0..131072, so writes can land far past the cell edge — and there is no way to read memory back (pour never takes payload bytes and there is no view op). Get code execution inside the service; the flag at /flag is readable only by the account the service process runs as, so printing it proves you own that process — and print the flag.
